title: Acts Chapter 19 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Acts chapter 19 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Acts Chapter 19 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Acts Chapter 19.

questions.question: Where did Paul come to after passing through the upper coasts?
questions.explanation: Paul came to Ephesus after passing through the upper coasts, as stated in Acts 19:1.

questions.question: True or False: The disciples that Paul found in Ephesus had heard of the Holy Ghost.
questions.explanation: The disciples said they had not so much as heard whether there be any Holy Ghost, according to Acts 19:2.

questions.question: What type of baptism did the disciples say they had received?
questions.explanation: The disciples answered that they were baptized unto John's baptism, which was a baptism of repentance, as mentioned in Acts 19:3-4.

questions.question: True or False: Paul laid his hands on the disciples, and they received the Holy Ghost.
questions.explanation: Paul laid his hands upon them, and the Holy Ghost came on them, as stated in Acts 19:6.

questions.question: After Paul spoke in the synagogue, how long did he continue there?
questions.explanation: Paul spake boldly in the synagogue for the space of three months, according to Acts 19:8.

questions.question: How many men were there among the disciples Paul found?
questions.explanation: The text states that all the men were about twelve, according to Acts 19:7.

questions.question: True or False: Paul was in Ephesus for a short time before leaving.
questions.explanation: Paul continued in Ephesus for the space of two years, as stated in Acts 19:10.

questions.question: What special miracles were wrought by Paul?
questions.explanation: God wrought special miracles by the hands of Paul, including handkerchiefs healing the sick, as mentioned in Acts 19:11-12.

questions.question: What did the seven sons of Sceva attempt to do?
options: Baptize in the name of Jesus
questions.explanation: The seven sons of Sceva attempted to call over those with evil spirits the name of the Lord Jesus, according to Acts 19:13.

questions.question: True or False: The evil spirit recognized Jesus and Paul but did not know the sons of Sceva.
questions.explanation: The evil spirit acknowledged Jesus and Paul but asked, 'Who are ye?' referring to the sons of Sceva, as stated in Acts 19:15.

questions.question: In Acts 19, which event occurs FIRST?
options: Paul lays hands on the disciples
The evil spirit speaks to the sons of Sceva
questions.explanation: The baptism of the disciples in the name of the Lord Jesus happens first before the other listed events, as seen in Acts 19:5.

medium.title: Acts Chapter 19 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Acts Chapter 19 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did the evil spirit say when confronted by the sons of Sceva?
options: I know Jesus and Paul, but who are you?
I am the evil spirit of Diana.
I recognize you as holy men.
You have no power over me.
questions.correctAnswer: I know Jesus and Paul, but who are you?
questions.explanation: The evil spirit recognized Jesus and Paul but questioned the identity of the sons of Sceva, indicating their lack of authority. This is found in Acts 19:15.

questions.question: How did the man possessed by the evil spirit react to the sons of Sceva?
options: He defeated them, causing them to flee naked and wounded.
questions.correctAnswer: He defeated them, causing them to flee naked and wounded.
questions.explanation: The possessed man overcame the sons of Sceva and prevailed against them, leading them to flee in a shameful state. This is detailed in Acts 19:16.

questions.question: What was the reaction of the people in Ephesus after the incident with the evil spirit?
options: They praised the sons of Sceva.
Fear fell on them, and the name of the Lord Jesus was magnified.
questions.correctAnswer: Fear fell on them, and the name of the Lord Jesus was magnified.
questions.explanation: The account of the defeated sons of Sceva led to great fear among the people, and it caused the name of Jesus to be honored. This is mentioned in Acts 19:17.

questions.question: What action did many believers take after hearing about the events with the evil spirit?
options: They burned their scrolls of curious arts.
questions.correctAnswer: They burned their scrolls of curious arts.
questions.explanation: Upon believing, many who practiced magic brought their books together and burned them, demonstrating their commitment to follow Christ. This is recorded in Acts 19:19.

questions.question: How much did the books burned by the believers cost?
questions.explanation: The total value of the burned books was significant, amounting to fifty thousand pieces of silver, indicating the seriousness of their repentance. This is stated in Acts 19:19.

questions.question: What was the result of the word of God after these events in Ephesus?
options: It was ignored by the people.
It caused division among the believers.
It was suppressed by the authorities.
questions.explanation: The word of God flourished and gained strength in Ephesus after the believers’ actions and the miracles performed by Paul. This is confirmed in Acts 19:20.

questions.question: What did Paul plan to do after his time in Asia?
options: Travel to Jerusalem and then to Rome.
questions.correctAnswer: Travel to Jerusalem and then to Rome.
questions.explanation: Paul had a clear plan to visit Jerusalem and expressed a desire to see Rome as well, demonstrating his commitment to spread the Gospel. This is found in Acts 19:21.

questions.question: What caused a stir in Ephesus during Paul's ministry?
options: The building of a new temple.
The actions of Demetrius, the silversmith.
questions.correctAnswer: The actions of Demetrius, the silversmith.
questions.explanation: Demetrius stirred up trouble among the craftsmen due to Paul's influence on people's beliefs about idols, indicating the economic threat to their trade. This is explained in Acts 19:24.

questions.question: What was Demetrius concerned about regarding Paul’s teachings?
options: They promoted the worship of Diana.
They undermined their craft and the worship of Diana.
They were not popular with the people.
questions.correctAnswer: They undermined their craft and the worship of Diana.
questions.explanation: Demetrius claimed that Paul’s teachings posed a threat to their livelihood and the honor of the goddess Diana, reflecting the cultural conflict. This is stated in Acts 19:26.

questions.question: What was the crowd's reaction to Demetrius' speech?
options: They shouted, 'Great is Diana of the Ephesians.'
They began to debate amongst themselves.
questions.correctAnswer: They shouted, 'Great is Diana of the Ephesians.'
questions.explanation: The crowd was incited to rally in support of Diana, showcasing their devotion and anger against Paul's influence. This is found in Acts 19:28.

questions.question: True or False: The assembly in Ephesus was orderly and knew clearly why they had come together.
questions.explanation: The assembly was filled with confusion, and most did not understand the reason for the gathering, as indicated in Acts 19:32.

questions.question: True or False: The town clerk defended Paul and the other believers in the assembly.
questions.explanation: The town clerk defended Paul and clarified that they had not committed any crime, urging the crowd to remain peaceful. This is found in Acts 19:37.

questions.question: True or False: Paul was allowed to enter the theater to speak to the crowd.
questions.explanation: Paul wanted to enter the theater, but his disciples did not allow him to do so for his safety. This is mentioned in Acts 19:30.

hard.title: Acts Chapter 19 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Acts Chapter 19.

questions.question: What did Paul ask the disciples when he found them in Ephesus?
options: Have ye received the Holy Ghost since ye believed?
questions.correctAnswer: Have ye received the Holy Ghost since ye believed?
questions.explanation: Paul asked the disciples about the Holy Ghost, indicating its importance in their faith journey (Acts 19:2).

questions.question: What was the response of the disciples concerning the Holy Ghost?
options: We have not so much as heard whether there be any Holy Ghost.
We are filled with the Holy Ghost.
We have heard of the Holy Spirit.
We believe in the Holy Ghost.
questions.correctAnswer: We have not so much as heard whether there be any Holy Ghost.
questions.explanation: The disciples were unaware of the Holy Ghost, which highlights their incomplete understanding of the faith (Acts 19:2).

questions.question: How many men were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus according to Paul?
questions.explanation: The text explicitly states that all the men were about twelve (Acts 19:7).

questions.question: What significant event happened when Paul laid his hands on the disciples?
options: They spoke with tongues and prophesied.
questions.correctAnswer: They spoke with tongues and prophesied.
questions.explanation: Upon receiving the Holy Ghost, they began to speak in tongues and prophesy, demonstrating a clear sign of the Spirit's presence (Acts 19:6).

questions.question: What did Demetrius claim was at risk due to Paul's teachings?
questions.explanation: Demetrius warned that Paul's teachings were endangering the worship of Diana, indicating the cultural and economic implications (Acts 19:27).

questions.question: What was the reaction of the people when Demetrius spoke against Paul?
questions.explanation: The crowd was filled with confusion and wrath after hearing Demetrius, leading to chaos in the city (Acts 19:28).

questions.question: Who did the assembly rush to catch during the uproar in Ephesus?
questions.explanation: The assembly caught Gaius and Aristarchus, who were companions of Paul, reflecting the hostility towards his followers (Acts 19:29).

questions.question: Which chief of Asia sent a message to Paul urging him not to enter the theatre?
options: Certain of the chief of Asia
questions.correctAnswer: Certain of the chief of Asia
questions.explanation: Certain chief friends of Paul sent a message to protect him from the mob's wrath, showing concern for his safety (Acts 19:31).

questions.question: For how long did the uproar in Ephesus last according to the townclerk's remarks?
questions.explanation: The people cried out for about two hours, which indicates their fervent devotion to Diana (Acts 19:34).

questions.question: What does the term 'curious arts' refer to in Acts 19?
questions.explanation: Curious arts pertain to practices of magic, which many confessed and renounced after believing (Acts 19:19).

questions.question: The townclerk said the Ephesians were worshippers of which goddess?
questions.explanation: The townclerk affirmed that the city was known for worshipping Diana, a central figure in Ephesus's identity (Acts 19:35).

questions.question: True or False: The assembly in Ephesus was completely united in their purpose.
questions.explanation: The assembly was confused, and many did not know why they were gathered, indicating disunity (Acts 19:32).

questions.question: True or False: Paul was advised by his disciples to enter the theatre.
questions.explanation: His disciples urged him not to enter the theatre due to the danger posed by the crowd (Acts 19:30).

questions.question: Which Old Testament book is echoed in the themes of renunciation of false gods and practices seen in Acts 19?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy emphasizes the importance of renouncing false gods, paralleled by the burning of curious arts books in Acts 19:19.

questions.question: The word 'Diana' in Acts 19 is connected to which Greek term that signifies 'divine' or 'heavenly'?
questions.explanation: Diana's name is derived from 'Theia', a term associated with divinity, reflecting her status as a goddess in Ephesus (Acts 19:35).

theological.title: Acts Chapter 19 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Acts Chapter 19 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What did Paul ask the disciples he found in Ephesus regarding the Holy Ghost?
options: Have ye received the Holy Ghost since ye believed?
Do you believe in Jesus Christ?
Have you been baptized in water?
Do you know about the resurrection?
questions.correctAnswer: Have ye received the Holy Ghost since ye believed?
questions.explanation: Paul asked them if they had received the Holy Ghost since they believed, indicating the importance of the Holy Spirit in the believer's life (Acts 19:2).

questions.question: How many men were baptized by Paul in the name of the Lord Jesus?
questions.explanation: The text specifies that all the men involved were about twelve, indicating a small but significant group of early believers (Acts 19:7).

questions.question: What type of miracles did God perform through Paul in Ephesus?
questions.explanation: The scripture states that God wrought special miracles by the hands of Paul, affirming God's power to manifest through His apostles (Acts 19:11).

questions.question: What was the significant outcome of the burning of curious arts books?
options: It demonstrated the power of God
It resulted in a financial loss
questions.correctAnswer: It demonstrated the power of God
questions.explanation: The act of burning these books showed a powerful rejection of idolatry and an affirmation of the supremacy of God's word, as many believed and confessed their deeds (Acts 19:18-19).

questions.question: What was Demetrius' primary concern regarding Paul's influence in Ephesus?
questions.explanation: Demetrius worried that Paul's preaching was turning people away from the worship of Diana, which threatened their financial gain from making silver shrines (Acts 19:24-25).

questions.question: What did the evil spirit say when confronted by the sons of Sceva?
questions.explanation: The evil spirit acknowledged Jesus and Paul, but questioned the identity of the exorcists, illustrating the authority of Jesus and His apostles over demonic forces (Acts 19:15).

questions.question: What attribute of God is demonstrated through the miracles performed by Paul?
questions.explanation: The special miracles performed by Paul reflect God's omnipotence, demonstrating His sovereign power over sickness and evil spirits (Acts 19:11).

questions.question: What was the reaction of the city regarding the stir caused by Paul’s teachings?
options: They welcomed him with open arms
questions.explanation: The assembly was confused and did not know why they had gathered, showing the chaotic impact of the uproar caused by the conflict between belief in Christ and idol worship (Acts 19:32).

questions.question: What doctrine is illustrated by Paul’s separation from those who opposed his teachings?
questions.explanation: Paul's decision to separate from those who spoke evil of the way signifies a principle of church discipline, where believers are called to avoid unrepentant sin among them (Acts 19:9).

questions.question: How did Paul’s ministry in Ephesus affect the surrounding region?
options: It caused a decline in trade
questions.explanation: The text notes that all who dwelt in Asia heard the word of the Lord Jesus, indicating the extensive impact of Paul's ministry during his time in Ephesus (Acts 19:10).

questions.question: What does Acts 19:20 suggest about the growth of the word of God?
questions.explanation: The passage emphasizes that the word of God grew mightily and prevailed, indicating a significant advance of the gospel in the region (Acts 19:20).

questions.question: What historical significance does the mention of Diana in this chapter have?
options: She represented the prosperity of Ephesus
She was a symbol of Roman power
questions.correctAnswer: She represented the prosperity of Ephesus
questions.explanation: Diana was a major goddess in Ephesus, and her worship was integral to the economic and cultural identity of the city, which is highlighted in Demetrius' speech (Acts 19:27).

questions.question: How does the conflict between Paul and Demetrius highlight the theme of idolatry in Acts 19?
options: It shows the power of false gods
It emphasizes the futility of idol worship
It demonstrates the unity of belief
It encourages the worship of many gods
questions.correctAnswer: It emphasizes the futility of idol worship
questions.explanation: Demetrius' concern about the loss of worship for Diana illustrates the futility and danger of idolatry, as Paul's message challenges the legitimacy of such idols (Acts 19:26).

questions.question: What does the phrase 'the way' refer to in the context of Acts 19?
questions.explanation: The term 'the way' commonly refers to the early Christian faith and teachings, which Paul was actively promoting and defending against opposition (Acts 19:9).

questions.question: In Acts 19:41, what action did the town clerk take after addressing the crowd?
questions.explanation: The town clerk calmed the crowd and dismissed them, showing his authority and the desire to prevent further chaos (Acts 19:41).
